lines: How does Singapore hold back the sea?
With pumps that can empty an Olympic pool in under 9 seconds.
In 2008, it built a 350-meter dam across the mouth of its downtown bay.
Nine gates keep the sea out.
Behind them, rain from 100 square kilometers of city turned salt water into a freshwater reservoir.
And when heavy rain hits at high tide, the gates stay shut and seven giant pumps push it out to sea.
So the sea downtown became drinking water. That's how Singapore holds back the sea.
